summary: Daniela Bevilacqua specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned doctorates from Sapienza University of Rome and Paris Nanterre University, and was attested as a postdoctoral research fellow at SOAS University of London in 2020.
Daniele Cuneo works in Indology and philosophy. He held a post at the University of Paris (attested 2018) and is attested as a faculty member at the University of Texas at Austin in 2026.
Danielle Feller is an Indologist who completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne in 2001 under Johannes Bronkhorst, and also studied under Ganesh Umakant Thite.
Danielle Jacquart is a historian who studied at the École des chartes (~1967–1971). She held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from around 1990 to 2016.
Danping Long works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She is attested in 2026 as a doctoral student at both the University of Munich and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Indologist Danuta Stasik studied under Maria Krzysztof Byrski at the University of Warsaw (~1975–1980). She remained at the University of Warsaw, holding posts in 1980 (prof. dr hab.) and 1986.
Daoquan Yu was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who studied under Jacques Bacot. He served as professor of Tibetan language and literature at Minzu University of China.

Dasharatha Sharma studied at the University of Delhi and taught history and Indology. He held posts at Hindu College, University of Delhi (~1959–1966), Jai Narain Vyas University (1966), and directed the Rajasthan Oriental Research Institute (~1966–1976).

Daud Ali studied at William & Mary and the University of Chicago under Ronald Inden. He taught history at SOAS (~1996–2009) and became associate professor of South Asian history at the University of Pennsylvania in 2009.

Daud Rahbar studied at Government College University, Lahore, and Cambridge. He held positions at University of the Punjab, Oriental College, McGill, Ankara University, and University of Wisconsin-Madison, before serving at Boston University (~1968–1998).
David A. Dilworth works in philosophy and Japanology. He studied under Masao Abe and Valdo H. Viglielmo (1968).

David A. Hall studied under Shōshin Ichishima and earned his doctorate at UC Berkeley (1990). He was a visiting scholar at Taisho University (1977) and Chair of Science, Engineering and Technology at Montgomery College (attested 2019).
David Azzopardi, an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under Kate Crosby (attested 2010).

David B. Gray earned his Ph.D. from Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and Ryuichi Abe. He completed a postdoctoral fellowship at Rice University and held an associate professorship at Santa Clara University (attested 2008–2017).
David Brown was a religious studies and Indology scholar who studied at Magdalene College, Cambridge (~1782–1785). He served as Provost of Fort William College in 1800.
David Bubna-Litic earned a PhD from Western Sydney University and served as Lecturer in Strategic Management and Responsible Business at the University of Technology Sydney (both attested 2000).

David Burton, a specialist in Buddhist studies and philosophy, completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Bristol (1994–1997). In 2010, he was attested as Senior Lecturer at Canterbury Christ Church University.

David Dean Shulman studied at Hebrew University and earned his doctorate at SOAS under John Ralston Marr. He held appointments at Hebrew University (from 1976) and served as Director of the Israel Institute for Advanced Studies (1992–1998).

David Drewes studied at Lawrence University, UW-Madison, and UVA (PhD 2006 under Karen Christina Lang). He taught at UVA, Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2006), and the University of Manitoba (attested 2009–2010).

David E. Cooper studied at St Edmund Hall and lectured in philosophy at Oxford (1967). He was Professor of Philosophy at Durham University (1986–2008) and Distinguished International Visiting Professor at Peking University (2022).
